info.name: Pact of the Concept
info.description: Pact of the Concept warlock subclass — ATÉRIOR.
info.author: Falling-Cats

description.p: Not a bargain, not a patron who wants anything from you — a passive, half-second brush of attention from one of the seven fundamental principles reality runs on, caught only because your own nature already resonated with what it is.

Reality itself runs on seven fundamental principles — Creation, Ending, Memory, Transformation, Desire, Chaos, Sacrifice — vast enough and old enough that mortal minds only ever manage rough, cultural approximations of what they actually are. They don't converse. They don't bargain. But every so often, briefly, one of them looks somewhere, and if a person's own life already resonates with whatever that Concept fundamentally is, that brief, passing attention is enough to leave something behind.
Choose which Concept noticed you: the Weaver, the Endling, the Scribe, the Mask, the Hunger, the Stranger, or the Thorn.

description.p: Whenever you roll one or more damage dice as part of an attack or spell, you can remove one of those dice and roll it separately, recording the result as your Reserve. You can also generate a Reserve by reducing an ability check's result by your Charisma modifier before it resolves, using the amount removed as your Reserve instead. Either way, you can generate a Reserve this way a number of times per Long Rest equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1). If you gain a new Reserve while already holding one, it replaces the old.

As a free action on your turn, or as a Reaction when you or a creature you can see makes an attack roll, ability check, saving throw, or damage roll, you can expend your Reserve to add its value to that roll before the outcome is known. Once spent, it's gone. If the die you removed came from a hit against a creature you've Understood, roll it twice and keep the higher as your Reserve.

Playing It. Spending your Reserve is free — it doesn't count against your Long Rest limit. Only generating a new one does. You can bank one, hold it as long as you want, and cash it in on someone else's roll entirely.

sheet.description: Remove one damage die from an attack or spell (or reduce an ability check by your Charisma modifier before it resolves) and bank the result as your Reserve. You can generate a Reserve this many times per Long Rest, replacing any Reserve you already hold. Spending it — adding its value to any roll before the outcome is known, free or as a Reaction — costs nothing extra.
